subject: general
question: Why is carbon monoxide an air pollutant?

options.text: Because it is converted into carbon dioxide
Because it is present in vehicle exhaust
Because it is reduces oxygen carrying capacity of blood** **

solution:
**​​​**The correct answer is** Because it reduces the oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood. **

**Explanation:**

 
• The haemoglobin in our blood takes oxygen to different parts of our body from the Lungs.
 
• The oxygen affinity of haemoglobin is less than that of CO affinity towards haemoglobin.
 
• When we inhale air polluted with carbon monoxide (CO), carbon monoxide (CO) will combine with haemoglobin, forming carboxyhemoglobin in the blood and Stopping oxygen transport.
 
• The binding of carbon monoxide to haemoglobin, forming carboxyhemoglobin, reduces the amount of oxygen available to the heart muscle and other tissues for synthesizing ATP.
 
• It is a pollutant for humans since it reacts with Haemoglobin. It is harmful when breathed since it displaces oxygen in the blood and deprives the heart, brain and other important organs.
